channel.name: Beyond Orbit
channel.niche: Faceless space & universe documentaries — black holes, exoplanets, cosmic scale, unexplained signals — narrated over real NASA/ESA public-domain imagery
channel.audience: USA viewers who binge space documentaries and 'what if' cosmic scenarios
channel.cta: Subscribe — a new deep-space story every week.
channel.comment: LONG-FORM space documentary channel (16:9). This is the watch-hours engine: Shorts feed watch time does NOT count toward the 4,000-hour YPP threshold, but long-form watch time DOES. Each long-form video also spawns one vertical Short (see 'shorts' below) for discovery/subs. To re-brand, change name/handle/tagline/cta here AND the channel name on YouTube.

topics.comment: Topics come from topics/space_bank.json (50 hand-written viral angles, each with a hook, script beats, chapters and suggested NASA visuals). If GEMINI_API_KEY is set and use_gemini=true, the script is expanded/fresh-written per run using the bank entry as the brief (falls back to the built-in beat templates on any error). order='sequence' walks the bank 1,2,3...; 'random' picks no-repeat random.

script.comment: 7-LAYER HOOK SYSTEM. cold_open_seconds: first line must shock — NO logo, NO 'hey guys', NO intro. promise_at_seconds: state what the viewer gets by the end. open_loop_every_seconds: plant an unresolved question every ~55s so the viewer cannot leave. words_per_minute=150 is the natural edge-tts documentary pace, used to estimate runtime from word count. IMPORTANT — READ THIS: the topic bank stores a BRIEF (a hook plus research beats), not a finished script. With GEMINI_API_KEY set, Gemini turns that brief into a full 1500-2200 word (~12 min) script and everything works as intended. WITHOUT a Gemini key the offline template mode only reaches about 2-3 minutes, because expanding terse beats into 1500 words locally would be pure filler — and filler both destroys retention and is precisely what YouTube's inauthentic-content policy penalises. So min_publishable_minutes=6 acts as a safety gate: generate.py SKIPS a topic (without burning it from the rotation) rather than publishing a 2-minute stub as a documentary. Set allow_short_publish=true only if you deliberately want short videos out.

tts.comment: edge-tts = free Microsoft neural voices, NO API key. For documentaries keep rotate_voices=FALSE — one consistent narrator voice builds channel identity (the opposite of Shorts, where rotation avoids 'templated content' flags). rate='+4%' is a calm documentary pace (Shorts use +14%). pitch='-2Hz' adds a little authority. Andrew/Brian are the most documentary-sounding US male voices.

video.comment: 1440p (2560x1440) is the DEFAULT and the recommended setting — YouTube encodes 1440p and above with the better VP9 codec, so even a viewer watching at 1080p sees a sharper picture than a 1080p upload. Set resolution='4k' for true 4K, but note free GitHub runners have NO GPU: 4K at preset='fast' takes ~45-90 min, and 4K at preset='medium' can exceed the 6-hour job limit. shot_seconds_min/max = PATTERN INTERRUPT: the visual changes every 4-8s so the viewer's brain never settles. ken_burns adds slow zoom/pan to still NASA images so they never look like a static slideshow.

captions.comment: For LONG-FORM, burn_in defaults to FALSE — burned-in captions look amateurish on a 12-minute documentary and block the visuals. Instead we upload a real .srt caption track to YouTube (better for SEO and accessibility, and viewers can toggle it). The Short DOES get big burned-in karaoke captions (see shorts.captions_*). Set burn_in=true only if you specifically want them baked into the long-form.

chapters.comment: YouTube chapters require the FIRST timestamp to be 00:00 and at least 3 chapters, each 10s or longer. Chapters increase watch time (viewers re-watch sections) and add SEO keywords to the description.

thumbnail.comment: 1280x720 is the YouTube standard. max_words=5 — on a phone the thumbnail is ~120px wide, so more than 5 words is unreadable. 3 variants are generated per video (different crop/layout/hook wording) so you can pick the best; variant 1 is uploaded automatically. Space thumbnails win on SCALE CONTRAST (tiny Earth next to a huge object) since there is no face to use.

shorts.comment: Each documentary is auto-clipped into 'count' vertical Shorts. The highest-scoring NON-OVERLAPPING ~40s windows are picked from the narration word timings (sentence-aligned, outro excluded), cropped to 1080x1920, and given big burned-in karaoke captions. count=3 matters: at 3 long-form uploads a week, one Short each would only be 3 Shorts a week, which is far too slow to build subscribers — 3 each gives roughly daily Shorts from the same single render. stagger_days=1 spreads them over consecutive days via publishAt so they do not all land at once. Division of labour: the Shorts are the DISCOVERY engine (subs), the long-form is the WATCH-HOURS engine. Shorts feed watch time does NOT count toward the 4,000-hour threshold, which is precisely why the long-form exists.

nasa.comment: NASA content generally is NOT subject to copyright in the US — that is this channel's unfair advantage: broadcast-quality space footage with effectively zero Content ID risk. SOURCES: 'images_api' (images-api.nasa.gov) is the only source enabled by default. It needs no API key, is a documented stable endpoint, and already mirrors a large amount of SVS and JPL material. You may add 'svs' to this list, but be aware modules/nasa_fetch.py deliberately does NOT download from SVS: its JSON endpoint is not published as a versioned public API, so we do not want a silent shape change to break every render. TWO HARD RULES are enforced in nasa_fetch.py: (1) block_keywords rejects the NASA logo/insignia/meatball/worm, which may NOT be used because doing so implies NASA endorses this channel — matching is word-boundary based so 'wormhole' and 'sealed' are not false positives; (2) any asset whose metadata names a third-party rights holder (copyright, Getty, 'all rights reserved', etc.) is skipped, because some NASA pages embed licensed music or contractor footage. ESA/Hubble and ESO material is CC BY 4.0, so attribution is auto-added to the description by modules/metadata.py.

youtube.comment: category_id 28 = Science & Technology. TIMING: publish at 2:00 PM ET on Thu/Fri/Sat — that single slot catches the US after-school/after-work window, the 7-11 PM ET evening peak, AND the next morning. CRITICAL: upload_lead_hours=5 means the file is uploaded 5 hours BEFORE publish time as PRIVATE with status.publishAt set. Without this a 1440p/4K video goes live while YouTube is still processing, so the first hour — the single most important hour for the algorithm — is served at 360p. title_hashtags: only the FIRST 3 hashtags render above the title, so we pick deliberately.
